messages:
Lena: heads up — noticed a 9-12% p99 latency bump on canary after kv-prefetch rollout yesterday. metric spike around 11:20p UTC, serving nodes in us-west-2 only.

Marc: ack. which canary tag? the rollout that landed PR #4231?

Lena: yes @Marc — canary tag `prefetch-v2-canary-3`. CPU not saturated, but we see more GPU stalls + longer kernel tails in the flame graph. link: https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/abcd

Rachel: paging @Austin and @Samir — looks like the prefetch eviction change might be triggering extra cache churn under certain seq-lengths. I can reproduce locally with `tests/perf/kv_prefetch_smoke.py` using seq=1024.

Austin: interesting. I ran the smoke with `--seq 1024 --clients 50` and saw the same tail. stack trace shows `kv_lookup` spikes when prefetch window overlaps with batching flush.

Samir: can you paste the minimal repro command? I want to run it against the canary cluster.

Rachel: repro: \n```\npython tests/perf/kv_prefetch_smoke.py --seq 1024 --clients 50 --model rwd/opt-6.7b --prefetch-windowsize 4\n```

Lena: also seeing more lock contention in logs: `runtime/kv/cache.go:87` shows repeated `cache.mu` waits. thrown ~2s per stall in some requests. snippet: `WARN cache: eviction wait 1.9s key=...`

eng-runtime-bot: Canary rollout `prefetch-v2-canary-3` -> 60% nodes (us-west-2) at 2026-03-15T23:18:21Z. Health: degraded (latency > SLO) since 2026-03-15T23:20:10Z.

Marc: hypothesis: prefetch aggressiveness + batch flush timing = transient larger KV footprints causing more frequent evictions, which forces memcopy/kernels to reload KV pages mid-request.

Austin: mitigation idea: reduce prefetch windowsize to 2 for canary, and add a small jitter to batch flush timing to avoid synchronization. low-risk rollback path: revert PR #4231 on canary only.

Samir: I'll spin a quick canary with windowsize=2 and jitter=on. ETA ~20m. I'll post results.

Lena: thanks — please also capture traces for any p99 requests and attach traces id. I collected one: trace://tr/0a1b2c (p99 at 23:21:03).

Rachel: quick note for owners: assign follow-ups -> kernel perf (Marc), kv-cache heuristics (Rachel), rollout tooling (Samir).

Marc: opened a short RFC in #4239 describing possible kernel prefetch backpressure handling. cc @Rachel.

Samir: canary with windowsize=2 deployed to us-west-2 (tag `prefetch-v2-canary-3a`). preliminary: p99 back down ~4%, still slightly up vs baseline. full results in 10m.

eng-runtime-bot: Deployment event: `prefetch-v2-canary-3a` -> completed at 2026-03-15T23:43:00Z.

Lena: initial observation: p99 improved to +3% (was +9-12%). good direction. leave canary running for another 2h and collect histograms.

Marc: will add a micro-benchmark that reproduces the kernel tail (kernel harness + randomized prefetch jitter). PR incoming shortly.

Rachel: I'll schedule a follow-up async doc in docs/perf/kv-prefetch-rollout.md with findings and recommended defaults.

Samir: wrote the rollout note in the canary runbook and flagged that the default windowsize should be conservative on Dedicated pools.

Lena: thanks everyone. action items: Marc -> kernel harness PR, Rachel -> doc + repro attestation, Samir -> update rollout defaults + monitor, Austin -> help validate traces. circle back ~2026-03-16T02:00:00Z. :thumbsup:
